newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank reports 24 percent rise in 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank reports 24 percent rise in 1996 profit.

text.p: Commerzbank AG, Germany's third-largest commercial bank, Monday reported a 24 percent rise in net profits for 1996, citing what it said were strong financial operations and strict cost control.
The bank also announced plans to seek shareholder approval for future capital-raising measures, including a possible 200 million mark ($118 million share issue).
In a statement released ahead of its annual results news conference on Tuesday, Commerzbank said its net profits for last year were 1.214 billion marks ($720 million).
Operating earnings rose 28.6 percent to 1.869 billion marks ($1.11 billion), while pre-tax earnings rose 50.5 percent to 1.795 billion ($1.07 billion).
"The basis for the strong earnings growth was dynamic financial operations accompanied by rigid cost discipline," Commerzbank said.
"On the other hand, the continued upward trend for corporate insolvencies led to a notable increase in provision for lending risks."
Commerzbank said it set aside 1.216 billion marks ($722 million) for lending risks after deducting earnings from securities held for liquidity purchases.
The bank also said it would seek approval for various capital measures at this year's shareholder meeting.

Authorisation will be sought for a 200 million mark share issue, a 50 million mark ($29.7 million) share issue for employees, up to two billion marks ($1.18 billion) in profit-sharing certificates and up to one billion marks ($593 million) for bonds with warrants and options.
All the authorisations will run through April 30 2002.
A slight increase in Commerzbank's share capital to some two billion marks ($1.19 billion) by the end of 1996 inflated the total dividend payout to 540 million marks ($320 million).

The bank noted this was more than double the amount distributed four years ago and also said it planned to allocate 650 million marks ($386 million) of retained earnings to its revenue reserves, up from 400 million marks ($237 million) the previous year.
